newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE UPS CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS FOR LISTING.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE UPS CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS FOR LISTING.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange increased by about 50 percent capital requirements for companies seeking listing on its main and parallel markets, the bourse's deputy president said on Thursday.
"The bourse's board decided to increase listing requirements by about 50 percent," Ryszard Czerniawski told a news conference.
Czerniawski said the new requirements would not apply to the bourse's third or so-called free market where now only one stock is listed, and to companies already trading on the exchange.
Under the present rules the market value of shares approved for bourse trade and the net asset value of a company seeking a main market listing have to be at least 24 million zlotys.
Companies seeking a parallel market listing have to meet a 12 million zloty threshold. The minimum capital requirement for third floor trading is four million zlotys.

Czerniawski said the new rules had to be approved by bourse shareholders and later by the Polish Securities Commission, and that the new requirements were likely to come into force in September. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
